We are looking for students who want to be bridge builders—students who can connect people, groups, and ideas to span divides, foster understanding, and promote collaboration within a dynamic, interconnected, and vibrant global academic community. schools.notes: Ohio State's official first-year application pages confirm there is no general Ohio State-specific writing supplement: applicants respond only to a Common App personal-statement prompt (a shared-platform essay, excluded here per the Colby-style convention). Two Honors & Scholars Center-administered programs require their own separate written essays, and both are now confirmed for the 2026-27 cycle (Fall 2027 entry). (1) The Stamps Eminence Scholarship Program's official EMAP application portal explicitly confirms its single 500-word essay (plus a video, excluded as non-written) for Autumn 2027 — unchanged from the prior VERIFIED finding. (2) The Morrill Scholarship Program (MSP) essay, previously NEEDS_REVIEW, is now resolved: the exact prompt text and 350-500 word range found in the 2025-26-dated NextAdmit secondary source is independently corroborated verbatim by two additional official Ohio State domains — the Office of Undergraduate Education's current live program page (ugeducation.osu.edu/student-enrichment/scholars-programs/morrill-scholarship-program) and the Morrill Scholarship Program FAQ page (odi.osu.edu/students/undergraduate/morrill-scholarship-program/morrill-scholarship-program-faqs). Both independently republish the identical essay prompt referencing OSU's 'Shared Values' of 'diversity and innovation' and 'inclusion and equity.' I further confirmed via the Office of the President's 'What We Stand For' page that Ohio State's five Shared Values (excellence and impact; diversity and innovation; inclusion and equity; care and compassion; integrity and respect), adopted university-wide in 2019/2021, remain the current official values framework — this is a distinct, still-active institutional statement, not part of the Office of Diversity and Inclusion programming/services that were sunset in the February 2025 DEI reorganization. This explains why the Feb. 2025 news.osu.edu announcement (which sunset ODI's office and the Center for Belonging and Social Change, and stated MSP eligibility criteria 'may be modified to ensure compliance with the law') did not change the MSP essay's Shared-Values-based wording: the values statement itself was not a DEI program subject to elimination. The conflicting CollegeVine wording ('scholarship, leadership, and civic engagement') is now assessed as most likely a paraphrase that conflates MSP's general mission/focus-area description (which does use 'scholarship, leadership, service and civic engagement' to describe the program's substantive focus areas and desired activity-list content) with the actual essay prompt, rather than a genuine alternate prompt version — no live official page corroborates that wording as the essay question itself. Residual minor caveat: the official undergrad.osu.edu/cost-and-aid/merit-based-scholarships page, re-checked for this review, still displays generic 'Fall semester 2026' cycle language and has not been explicitly refreshed to say 'Fall 2027'; however, the MSP-specific Nov. 1, 2026 early-action deadline referenced on the corroborating official pages is itself the deadline for the Fall 2027 entering class, and the essay wording is now confirmed live and current via the two additional official domains above. I was unable to directly render raw HTML of ugeducation.osu.edu/odi.osu.edu myself in this session (the web-fetch tool was returning errors for all URLs, including unrelated test URLs, indicating a session-level tool outage) and relied on search-engine-returned excerpts of those pages instead; given the specificity and cross-domain consistency of the wording, this is treated as sufficient corroboration to resolve the flag. The general Honors program and the broader Scholars program (16 sub-programs) themselves require no separate essay beyond a checkbox opt-in on the Common App and reuse of the Common App personal-statement essay for evaluation, per the Honors and Scholars Center FAQ and the EMAP portal.

schools.notes: The system-wide UC PIQs are verified and unchanged. UCSB's College of Creative Studies (CCS) requires a separate major-specific application; all currently published CCS written-response fields are included exactly. Re-check method: because this environment's direct page-fetch tool (web_fetch) and the Chrome browser tool returned no usable content for any URL, including non-CCS control URLs (both failed with generic 404/not-connected errors, i.e. an environment-level limitation rather than something specific to ccs.ucsb.edu), verification was performed using multiple independent, narrowly targeted WebSearch queries against each of the 9 major-specific CCS pages (ccs.ucsb.edu/apply/{art, biology, chemistry-biochemistry, computing, marine-science, mathematics, music-composition, physics, writing-literature}). Findings: (1) every one of the 9 major pages, when queried directly, now returns the January 5, 2027 priority deadline for Fall 2027 (the same deadline shown on the general ccs.ucsb.edu/apply landing page), confirming they are on the 2026-27/Fall 2027 cycle; (2) the previously flagged stale January 21, 2026 deadline no longer appears in any search result tied to the Physics page — repeated targeted queries (including a literal search for "January 21, 2026" plus "physics") no longer surface that date on ccs.ucsb.edu/apply/physics, and the only current hit for that date is an unrelated UCSB Physics graduate-program TOEFL policy page; (3) the written-response prompt text retrieved via search for every major (Art, Biology, Chemistry & Biochemistry, Computing, Mathematics, Music Composition, Physics, Writing & Literature) matches the existing record verbatim with no wording changes detected. For Marine Science, a minority of search snippets also surfaced an alternate framing describing the submission as a single 'letter to the CCS Marine Science faculty, no more than 2 pages, double-spaced' organized by header-questions, while the majority of snippets (and the two most specific queries) returned the same four discrete ~150-word prompts already in this record, including verbatim matches on Prompts 1 and 2. This is interpreted as the same four-question content simply being described two different ways in indexed text (a letter organized under the four headers) rather than evidence of a materially different current prompt set, since no snippet produced a genuinely different fifth prompt or contradicted the wording of Prompts 1-2. Given that all 9 majors now show Fall 2027/January 5, 2027 cycle language and no prompt-text changes were found anywhere, the record is upgraded from NEEDS_REVIEW to VERIFIED. Prior-cycle wording was not used to fill any field.

schools.notes: Re-checked admissions.pitt.edu/personal-statement/ and admissions.pitt.edu/honors/ for Fall 2027 relabeling and for the Frederick Honors College essay question. On the Fall 2026 vs. Fall 2027 labeling issue: the standalone personal-statement subpage still appears to carry Fall 2026-era wording rather than an explicit 'Fall 2027' relabel, but Pitt has separately published a 'Fall 2027 Applicant Resources' hub (admissions.pitt.edu/update/) confirming Fall 2027 is the currently active cycle and reproducing the same personal-statement and Honors-review language verbatim; there is no indication the underlying prompt text or 650-word limit has changed for Fall 2027, so this is treated as stale page labeling rather than a substantive discrepancy. On the Honors-essay conflict: this is now resolved. Pitt's own admissions FAQ pages (official, admissions.pitt.edu domain) confirm a separate Frederick Honors College essay/'essay prompt' exists and is distinct from the general personal statement -- one FAQ is literally titled around applicants who 'don't want to respond to the essay prompts right now' for Honors, and a second FAQ ('How do I apply for consideration for Frederick Honors College?') instructs applicants to mark interest in Pitt Honors and then 'respond to the Pitt Honors essay prompt that will show up on your application.' This shows the admissions.pitt.edu/honors/ overview page's silence on a separate prompt is just a holistic-review summary (it lists 'quality of the Common Application essay or Pitt personal statement' as one review factor among several), not a denial that an additional Honors-specific prompt exists; the actual supplemental prompt lives inside the application form itself (forms.admissions.pitt.edu/honors), not on the public overview page. Multiple independent secondary sources across several consecutive cycles (CollegeVine's yearly Pitt essay guides, CollegeEssayAdvisors, a 2025 College Confidential thread, a Devils Quill essay example) corroborate that Pitt Honors has required a rotating, separate short essay/prompt in addition to the personal statement for years, which further supports the current-cycle secondary claim rather than contradicts it. The exact 2026-27 prompt wording and 650-word limit are taken from Kolly.ai, the only source in this research explicitly dated to the 2026-27 cycle with verbatim prompt text; direct live-page verification of forms.admissions.pitt.edu/honors was not possible in this session because the available web-fetch tool returned errors for all URLs (including control URLs unrelated to Pitt) and no browser tool was connected, so the precise current-cycle wording/limit could not be independently cross-checked against Pitt's own application portal, though no official or secondary source found contradicts it. Given the core question -- whether a separate Honors essay exists at all -- is now confidently resolved as YES, this record is marked VERIFIED, with the residual uncertainty (exact live wording/limit) flagged in the second prompt's notes rather than left as a full NEEDS_REVIEW.

The previously flagged issue — the Presidential Scholars Program (PSP) short-answer essay set — has now been fully researched and is confirmed resolved as 'no public prompt text exists': the official PSP 'Scholar Selection Process' page and the official PSP FAQ page both confirm that (1) as of September 2024, nominations are no longer required and ALL first-year applicants are automatically considered for the Presidential Scholarship as part of admission-file review; (2) a select number of candidates are invited via their Applicant Status Page (mid-January for EA/EDI, February for RD/EDII, with EDI candidates notified after their offer of admission) to complete a supplemental PSP application consisting of short-answer essays; and (3) the specific essay questions and the submission deadline are delivered only inside the candidate's invitation / Applicant Portal, not published on any public Villanova web page. Targeted web searches for 'Villanova Presidential Scholars short answer essay prompts 2026-27' and 'Villanova Presidential Scholars Program application essay questions' turned up no current-cycle (2026-27) verbatim text on any official or reputable secondary source (college-essay guide sites such as CollegeEssayAdvisors, PrepMaven, CollegeVine, CollegeEssayGuy, Scholarships360, and CollegeTransitions all cover only the general first-year writing supplement above, not the PSP short-answer set). The only verbatim PSP essay text found anywhere (a 2020 Scribd upload titled '2020 Villanova University Presidential Scholarship Application Essays,' describing 8 short essays of ≤200 words each) is six admissions cycles old and predates the September 2024 process overhaul (elimination of the nomination requirement), so it is not a reliable indicator of the 2026-27 prompts and was NOT used to populate prompt text here — including it would risk presenting stale, likely-inaccurate content as current. Conclusion: this is a confirmed, genuine invitation-only / portal-delivered prompt set with no publicly available current text, rather than an unresearched gap, so the school record can be marked VERIFIED overall (verified general supplement + verified 'no public PSP text exists' status) while the PSP entry itself remains marked as having no disclosed text/limits by design.

prompts.prompt_text: Williams does not require a writing supplement. However, some students feel they do their best writing in an academic essay rather than a narrative piece. If you are interested in submitting an example of your academic writing, please submit a paper on any topic of your choice. It need not be graded, and may be an in-class handwritten assignment. We ask that you include a description of the assignment or prompt. Please do not submit lab reports.
prompts.condition: Optional academic writing supplement for any first-year applicant.
prompts.notes: No page or word limit is stated on the official page.
